Definition: from G1839; a displacement of the mind, i.e. bewilderment, "ecstasy":--+ be amazed, amazement, astonishment, trance.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, ékstasis is the word for amazement, a trance. In Mark 5:42, the text says "for she was [of the age] of twelve years. And they were astonished with a great astonishment." In Mark 16:8, the text says "for they trembled and were amazed."
TheologicalSignificance: What ékstasis teaches me is that miracles are not magic tricks; they are God showing His hand in the open. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: The Resurrection; Jairus' Daughter and the Bleeding Woman; The Healing of the Paralytic
